paragraphs: Mixed time series contain both continuous measurements and discrete values. These two kinds of variables can have different distributions and patterns over time, making it difficult to learn useful representations of both together. MiTSformer addresses the resulting risk that a model represents one kind of variable more effectively than the other.

The approach starts from the possibility that discrete observations arise from underlying continuous quantities whose detail was lost through discretization. It attempts to recover representations of those quantities by combining temporal context at several scales. Guidance from the continuous variables, delivered through adversarial learning, helps adapt this aggregation process. Attention blocks then model relationships over time and across the recovered and originally continuous variables.

The authors report consistently leading results across five tasks: classification, regression, anomaly detection, filling missing values, and long-term forecasting. These findings support using a shared framework across different mixed-data problems. The interpretation of discrete variables as potentially hiding continuous information is a motivating premise of the method, rather than a claim that every discrete observation has such an origin.
neurips-2024-addressing-spatial-temporal.tldr: MiTSformer models mixed time series by recovering continuous representations behind discrete variables and aligning them with continuous measurements.

paragraphs: Some leading approaches to differentially private training require a matrix factorization before model training can begin. Finding a sufficiently good factorization involves a demanding numerical optimization problem. This preparation can impose substantial computational costs, even before accounting for the work of actually learning the model.

The paper introduces BSR, a factorization approach that uses properties of the standard matrix square root to avoid that bottleneck. It is designed to handle large problems efficiently. For stochastic gradient descent with momentum and weight decay, the authors derive analytical expressions, making the additional preparation cost negligible in this particular training setting.

The contribution includes bounds on approximation quality for both centralized and federated learning. These bounds provide theoretical support for replacing the expensive factorization procedure. Numerical experiments find that BSR-trained models perform comparably to the strongest existing methods while avoiding their factorization overhead. The stated benefit is therefore maintaining competitive model performance with much cheaper preparation; it does not mean that the underlying model training itself becomes computationally free.
neurips-2024-banded-square-root-matrix-f.tldr: BSR makes matrix factorization for private model training inexpensive while retaining performance comparable to leading methods.

paragraphs: Visual reprogramming adapts the interfaces of an existing vision model so it can solve a task with a different set of labels. A key challenge is interpreting the model's original output categories in terms of the new task. Existing label mappings can impose a one-to-one correspondence, potentially overlooking more complicated relationships between the two label sets.

Bayesian-guided Label Mapping replaces this rigid correspondence with a matrix of probabilities that is updated iteratively. Each entry describes a relationship between one original label and one downstream label. The values are guided by Bayesian conditional probabilities, using how the model's predictions and the downstream labels occur together on downstream examples.

Experiments with both pretrained vision models and vision-language models show better performance than existing mapping methods. The result supports representing label relationships probabilistically instead of forcing each category into a single pairing. Beyond improving adaptation, the matrix also provides a probabilistic way to analyze why visual reprogramming works: the original model's predictions can contain useful information even when its label vocabulary differs from the target task.
neurips-2024-bayesian-guided-label-mappi.tldr: Bayesian-guided Label Mapping improves visual reprogramming by learning probabilistic relationships between pretrained and downstream labels.

paragraphs: Video violence detection can confuse ordinary events with violent ones when their appearances are similar. The paper argues that representations learned only in Euclidean space can struggle to separate these ambiguous cases. It explores whether combining visual appearance with a geometry suited to hierarchical and complex event relationships can produce more discriminative features.

Dual-Space Representation Learning uses both Euclidean and hyperbolic spaces. The Euclidean component captures visual features, while the hyperbolic component develops contextual relationships among events. Its aggregation strategy progressively collects event information, selecting nodes using layer-sensitive hyperbolic associations constrained by a quantity called hyperbolic Dirichlet energy. This makes the selection of contextual information part of the representation-learning process.

Cross-space attention allows the two representations to exchange information before the final violence prediction. The intended benefit is that appearance and event relationships inform one another instead of remaining separate. The authors report that comprehensive experiments demonstrate the method's effectiveness for weakly supervised detection. This supports the combined representation strategy without establishing that hyperbolic geometry eliminates all ambiguity between normal and violent events.
neurips-2024-beyond-euclidean-dual-space.tldr: DSRL combines Euclidean visual features with hyperbolic event relationships to improve weakly supervised video violence detection.

paragraphs: Removing an object from an image requires generating a plausible replacement for the area it occupied. Diffusion-based inpainting can create realistic content, but realism alone does not ensure successful removal. Without suitable guidance, a model may generate the unwanted object again, undermining the purpose of the edit.

CLIPAway addresses this problem through the information used to guide inpainting. It uses CLIP embeddings that emphasize background regions while excluding foreground elements. By identifying representations that prioritize the surrounding background, the method aims to steer generation toward content appropriate for the cleared region. Its central contribution is therefore background-focused guidance for the editing process.

The authors describe improvements in inpainting accuracy and visual quality, with seamless object removal as the intended result. CLIPAway is presented as a plug-and-play component compatible with various diffusion-based inpainting approaches. It avoids relying on specialized training datasets or costly manual annotations, making its guidance mechanism easier to incorporate into existing methods. The abstract attributes its benefit to choosing the right conditioning information for removal, rather than merely improving the realism of generated images.
neurips-2024-clipaway-harmonizing-focuse.tldr: CLIPAway guides diffusion inpainting with background-focused CLIP embeddings to remove objects more effectively.

paragraphs: Species range maps estimate where a species occurs and support conservation, ecology, and environmental decisions. Traditional approaches depend on environmental measurements and reliable observations, which can be difficult to obtain in inaccessible or poorly resourced regions. This paper investigates how written descriptions can complement observations when estimating geographic ranges.

The framework combines millions of citizen science observations with Wikipedia descriptions of habitat preferences and geographic ranges for tens of thousands of species. It represents locations, species, and text in a common space. This shared representation learns spatial information globally and allows a range estimate to be produced from a species description without observations of that species.

On held-out species, these zero-shot estimates significantly outperform baselines and match estimates built from tens of observations. When observations are available, the language-informed representation also supplies a strong prior, improving range estimation with less data. Quantitative and qualitative analyses examine both range estimation and other spatial tasks. Together, the findings show how descriptive knowledge can support prediction for species with scarce observational records.
neurips-2024-combining-observational-dat.tldr: A shared representation of species, locations, and text enables useful range maps from descriptions and improves estimates when observations are scarce.

paragraphs: Safe reinforcement learning seeks policies that earn high long-term rewards while respecting safety constraints. Learning such policies can require many interactions with the environment because improving reward and reducing safety costs may pull training in different directions. Efficient Safe Policy Optimization, or ESPO, tackles this interaction cost by changing the sampling process.

ESPO uses three optimization modes: prioritize reward, prioritize cost reduction, or balance the two. It adjusts sampling dynamically according to the observed conflict between reward and safety gradients, which indicate how each objective would change the policy. This connects the way samples are collected to the current disagreement between the training objectives.

The paper provides theoretical guarantees for convergence and optimization stability, alongside improved sample-complexity bounds. On Safety-MuJoCo and Omnisafe, ESPO outperforms the evaluated primal and primal-dual baselines in reward and constraint satisfaction. It uses 25–29% fewer samples and reduces training time by 21–38%. These empirical results show that its efficiency gains accompany improvements in both objectives on the tested benchmarks.
neurips-2024-enhancing-efficiency-of-saf.tldr: ESPO adapts sampling to reward–safety conflicts, improving safe reinforcement learning while reducing samples and training time.

paragraphs: ESPACE compresses large language models by focusing on activations, the intermediate values produced during computation. It projects these values onto a calibrated set of principal components. This changes the starting point of compression from directly decomposing model weights to reducing the dimensions used to represent activations.

The authors state that this activation-centered formulation allows retraining without losing expressivity. During inference, regrouping matrix multiplications produces a weight decomposition as a consequence of the formulation. The paper also provides theoretical results for constructing projection matrices with optimal computational accuracy, linking the compression mechanism to its mathematical properties.

Experiments report 50% compression for GPT3, Llama2, and Nemotron4 with small accuracy losses, including a perplexity increase as low as 0.18 for GPT3-22B. At 20–40% compression, some GPT3 results improve on the baseline, including a perplexity decrease of up to 0.38 for GPT3-8B. ESPACE also reduces matrix-multiplication time and prompt-processing latency on existing hardware. These findings indicate practical computational benefits, while the varying accuracy outcomes distinguish preserved expressivity from unchanged measured performance.
neurips-2024-espace-dimensionality-reduc.tldr: ESPACE compresses language models through activation projections, achieving substantial compression with small accuracy losses and faster inference operations.

paragraphs: Graphical models describe relationships among variables and help researchers interpret high-dimensional data. However, estimating these relationships can produce biased outcomes when the data involve sensitive attributes or protected groups. This paper studies that issue across Gaussian, Covariance, and Ising models, placing fairness within the estimation problem itself.

The proposed framework combines a measure called pairwise graph disparity error with a tailored loss function. These components form a nonsmooth optimization problem with multiple objectives. The goal is to reduce disparities associated with protected attributes while retaining the model's ability to represent useful relationships in the data.

Experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets show reduced bias without undermining model performance in the reported evaluations. This matters because the framework addresses the structure being estimated, making fairness part of how relationships are learned. The evidence supports the compatibility of the chosen fairness objectives with effective graphical modeling in the tested settings. It does not establish that every possible definition of fairness can be satisfied simultaneously.
neurips-2024-fairness-aware-estimation-o.tldr: The paper integrates disparity measures into graphical-model estimation to reduce protected-group bias while preserving empirical performance.

paragraphs: Best-arm identification asks which of several options has the largest average reward, using samples to reach a specified confidence level. This paper studies a Bayesian version in which the underlying bandit model is drawn from a known prior. That setup differs from the usual frequentist treatment, where the model is fixed before sampling begins.

The authors show that established frequentist approaches, including track-and-stop and top-two algorithms, can perform arbitrarily poorly relative to the Bayesian objective. The result highlights that a sampling strategy effective for fixed problems need not use prior information efficiently when performance is assessed over models drawn from that prior.

The paper derives a lower bound on the expected number of samples and proposes a variant of successive elimination. Its sample requirement matches the lower bound up to a logarithmic factor, providing a near-matching theoretical benchmark rather than an exact equality. Simulations support the theoretical findings. The known prior is central to the setting and to understanding why a different algorithmic design can be advantageous.
neurips-2024-fixed-confidence-best-arm-i.tldr: A successive-elimination variant nearly matches the Bayesian sample lower bound, whereas standard frequentist methods can be arbitrarily suboptimal.

paragraphs: Learning to generate new views of real scenes requires seeing corresponding content from different perspectives. Collecting these correspondences at scale is difficult, and ordinary videos restrict the available views to those chosen during recording. The paper turns to 360-degree video as a source of more diverse views of real environments.

The authors introduce 360-1M, a dataset containing one million 360-degree videos, together with a process for efficiently finding corresponding frames from different viewpoints. They train a diffusion model called ODIN on this collection. The dataset and correspondence process address the data problem underlying scene-level view generation, extending beyond the object-centered data commonly used for learning 3D structure.

ODIN can generate novel views while moving the camera through a real-world environment, enabling it to infer scene geometry and layout. The authors also report improved results on standard novel-view synthesis and 3D reconstruction benchmarks. These findings connect the expanded training data to both view generation and reconstruction, supporting 360-degree video as a scalable source of multiview scene information.
neurips-2024-from-an-image-to-a-scene-le.tldr: ODIN learns from one million 360-degree videos to generate new scene viewpoints and improve 3D reconstruction.

paragraphs: Continual imitation learning builds a policy from demonstrations that arrive across different tasks and stages. Adapter-based methods add relatively few parameters for each new task and tend to reduce forgetting by separating task-specific parameters. That separation can also restrict how much knowledge is shared between demonstrations, limiting reuse when new tasks arrive.

IsCiL organizes adaptation around shareable skills that are learned incrementally. Demonstrations are mapped into a state representation space, where a prototype-based memory helps retrieve suitable skills for an input state. Each skill is learned through its corresponding adapter. This creates a mechanism for reusing relevant knowledge across demonstrations while retaining the parameter-efficient adapter structure.

Experiments on complex Franka-Kitchen and Meta-World tasks show robust task adaptation and sample efficiency, including the changing environments emphasized by the framework. The authors also demonstrate a simple extension for task unlearning. The results support treating reusable skills as the units of accumulated knowledge, allowing new tasks to draw on previously learned behavior instead of relying entirely on isolated task-specific adaptation.
neurips-2024-incremental-learning-of-ret.tldr: IsCiL incrementally learns retrievable, shareable skills in adapters to improve continual imitation learning and sample-efficient task adaptation.

paragraphs: Hidden discrete variables can influence observed data, but recovering their causal relationships is difficult when those relationships are nonlinear or structurally complex. Existing approaches often focus on linear models or impose restrictive latent structures. This paper develops a way to extract information about hidden structure from tables describing observed variables.

The key result connects the tensor rank of a contingency table to the minimum support of a particular conditioning set that d-separates the observed variables. That conditioning set need not belong to the observed set being examined. The connection makes rank informative about hidden variables, allowing the method to probe different collections of observations for evidence of latent structure.

Using this result, the authors give an algorithm for identifying latent causal structure under structural assumptions. Simulated experiments support its effectiveness. The contribution expands the kinds of discrete latent-variable models that causal discovery can address. Its identification claim remains conditional on those assumptions: the rank relationship supplies a useful route to discovery, rather than guaranteeing recovery of every possible hidden causal structure from discrete observations.
neurips-2024-learning-discrete-latent-va.tldr: Tensor-rank conditions reveal discrete latent variables and enable causal-structure identification under structural assumptions.

paragraphs: Adapting a text-to-image model to an unfamiliar concept does not always make it depict that concept accurately. The authors empirically connect failures on out-of-distribution concepts with poor training-data quality. Their framework, CATOD, addresses both the collection of useful examples and the schedule for training the adaptor.

CATOD follows an active-learning approach that accumulates high-quality data and uses it for adaptation. Its central scoring system balances two considerations: how aesthetically successful an image is and how well it matches the intended concept. These are distinct requirements, so the framework automatically weights them when deciding which data to select and when to train.

The paper includes theoretical analysis of this balancing mechanism and reports substantial empirical improvements over prior approaches. The stated results include an 11.10 increase in CLIP score and a 33.08% reduction in CMMD. These findings support making data selection an explicit part of concept adaptation. The approach matters because visually appealing training examples can still be inadequate if they fail to represent the concept the model is meant to learn.
neurips-2024-locating-what-you-need-towa.tldr: CATOD improves adaptation to unfamiliar visual concepts by balancing aesthetics and concept matching during data selection and adaptor training.

paragraphs: A model can answer knowledge-intensive questions using information acquired during training without learning new rules from its current surroundings. Mars targets the latter ability: interacting with an environment, inducing general knowledge from experience, and using that knowledge to make decisions. The paper calls this situated inductive reasoning.

Mars is an interactive environment whose terrain, survival conditions, and task dependencies are modified to introduce mechanisms that conflict with ordinary expectations. Agents must investigate the environment and discover useful rules for its particular context. This design makes the acquisition of local knowledge central to successful behavior, creating a test of adaptation through interaction.

Experiments show that the evaluated reinforcement-learning and language-model methods all struggle on the benchmark. The authors also explore Induction from Reflection, which prompts agents to infer rules from their past trajectories. Its superior performance supports the importance of explicitly reasoning over experience in Mars. The findings establish a challenging benchmark and a promising improvement, while leaving the broader goal of reliable situated reasoning open.
neurips-2024-mars-situated-inductive-rea.tldr: Mars tests whether agents can discover unfamiliar environmental rules through interaction, with reflection-based induction improving performance on the challenging benchmark.

paragraphs: A scene can be represented through precise geometric measurements or through the relationships among its components. This paper proposes Multiview Scene Graphs, a topological representation connecting places and objects. The task is to construct these graphs from images whose camera poses are not supplied, bringing multiple views into a shared relational description.

Building such a graph requires recognizing places, detecting objects, and deciding which object appearances across images refer to the same object. Limited fields of view and large viewpoint changes make these decisions difficult. The authors develop a dataset and annotations based on an existing public 3D dataset, along with an evaluation measure based on overlap between graph edges.

They also introduce a baseline built from pretrained vision models, using one Transformer decoder to combine place recognition and object association. Experiments show better performance than relevant existing baselines. The contribution therefore includes a representation, a benchmark, an evaluation measure, and a method, providing a concrete way to study scene understanding through connections among places and objects.
neurips-2024-multiview-scene-graph-7d0fb.tldr: Multiview Scene Graphs represent places and objects from unposed images, with a new benchmark and Transformer-based construction method.

paragraphs: Complex manipulation instructions often hide several smaller tasks. Breaking them into written steps can help, but text alone may leave ambiguity about the desired intermediate state. PERIA combines language planning with imagined subgoal images so that task decomposition includes both verbal reasoning and visual guidance.

The framework first performs lightweight multimodal alignment to help a multimodal language model perceive visual details alongside instructions. It then jointly instruction-tunes that model with a pretrained image-editing model, enabling instruction reasoning and subgoal-image generation together. A consistency alignment loss encourages the generated images to agree with their corresponding instructions and remain coherent.

That agreement matters because contradictory text and images could undermine the plan even if each appeared plausible separately. The loss is intended to mitigate hallucinations and semantic conflicts between the planning modes. Across three task domains, PERIA significantly outperforms competitive baselines in instruction-following accuracy and task success. These results support combining language and visual planning for the evaluated complex manipulation tasks, without implying that consistency errors are entirely eliminated.
neurips-2024-peria-perceive-reason-imagi.tldr: PERIA jointly plans verbal steps and imagined visual subgoals to improve instruction following and success in complex manipulation tasks.

paragraphs: This paper studies decision-making when the environment's transition rules are uncertain and performance is measured by long-run average cost. The objective is to choose a policy with the best worst-case cost across an uncertainty set of transition models. The analysis focuses on ergodic Markov chains, an explicit condition on the processes being studied.

The authors derive a subgradient of robust average cost and use it to build a robust policy mirror-descent algorithm. They also establish a bound comparing the costs of two policies and show that the objective satisfies the PL condition. These theoretical properties support convergence analysis even though the optimization problem involves uncertain dynamics.

With increasing step sizes, the method achieves linear convergence in the optimality gap. With a constant step size, it reaches an epsilon-optimal policy in order 1/epsilon iterations. The authors report a rate matching the best policy-based robust-MDP rates and claim the first global-optimum convergence result for general uncertainty sets in this average-cost setting. Simulations demonstrate the algorithm's performance alongside the theoretical guarantees.
neurips-2024-policy-optimization-for-rob.tldr: Robust policy mirror descent obtains global convergence guarantees for average-cost MDPs with general uncertainty sets in the ergodic setting.

paragraphs: When an option produces several kinds of reward, identifying the best option requires a rule for comparing reward vectors. This paper studies pure exploration under preferences represented by an ordering cone. The aim is to identify the most preferred policy with a specified confidence, using as few reward observations as possible.

The authors derive a lower bound on the samples needed to identify the most preferred arm. This bound shows how difficulty depends jointly on the geometry of the rewards and the preferences. For Gaussian rewards, they further describe that geometry and give a convex reformulation that can be solved through linear programming.

The reformulation guides an algorithm called Track and Stop with Preferences. A new concentration result for vector-valued rewards supports its analysis, leading to an upper bound that matches the sample-complexity lower bound. The contribution connects a theoretical measure of problem difficulty to an algorithm that achieves the corresponding bound. It also makes preferences an explicit part of sampling difficulty, rather than treating the reward vectors alone as sufficient to characterize the task.
neurips-2024-preference-based-pure-explo.tldr: Track and Stop with Preferences matches a sample-complexity lower bound that captures the geometry of preferences and vector-valued rewards.

paragraphs: PAC-Bayesian analysis provides frequentist guarantees while incorporating prior knowledge. Updating that prior from earlier data creates a difficulty: conventional final confidence bounds use only the data left after prior construction. Earlier observations can influence the prior, but their contribution to confidence is lost, limiting the usefulness of sequential updates.

Recursive PAC-Bayes preserves that confidence information through a decomposition of the expected loss of randomized classifiers. It expresses posterior loss as an excess relative to a scaled prior loss, plus that scaled prior loss itself. The prior term is then bounded recursively, carrying information from earlier stages into the final guarantee.

The authors also generalize split-kl and PAC-Bayes-split-kl inequalities to discrete random variables and use those results to bound excess losses. Their empirical evaluation reports substantial improvements over state-of-the-art methods. The central advance is a procedure whose sequential updates retain confidence information from earlier data. Here, no information loss refers to that statistical accounting across updates, specifically addressing the dependence on only the final batch that motivated the work.
neurips-2024-recursive-pac-bayes-a-frequ.tldr: Recursive PAC-Bayes updates priors sequentially while preserving earlier data's contribution to confidence guarantees.

paragraphs: Changing a sentence's wording can preserve its meaning, while a small semantic change can alter what it describes. SUGARCREPE++ tests whether language and vision-language models distinguish those situations. The motivation is that semantically equivalent sentences can receive diverging representations, making it unclear how well a model captures meaning beyond lexical form.

Each dataset example contains an image and three captions. Two captions express the same meaning using different wording, while a hard negative supplies a contrasting meaning. This creates a three-way test of semantic equivalence and difference. The authors evaluate models with different architectures, training objectives, and pretraining datasets to examine how broadly the challenge appears.

Results reveal difficulties with lexical versus semantic variation, particularly for object attributes and spatial relationships. Larger models, larger pretraining datasets, and multiple objectives are associated with better performance, but substantial room for improvement remains. Models that excel on compositionality benchmarks can still struggle here. The findings suggest that compositionality performance alone may not establish reliable understanding of changes in wording and meaning.
neurips-2024-sugarcrepe-dataset-vision-l.tldr: SUGARCREPE++ tests whether models distinguish changes in wording from changes in meaning and reveals gaps beyond existing compositionality benchmarks.

paragraphs: Graph Transformers allow broad interactions among nodes, but applying full attention across multiple graph snapshots can lose information about graph structure and time. SLATE addresses this problem by supplying an encoding that preserves both kinds of context. Its aim is to retain the advantages of Transformer attention while representing how the graph is organized and changes.

The method turns a discrete-time dynamic graph into a multilayer graph. It then uses spectral properties of the associated supra-Laplacian matrix to construct the spatiotemporal encoding. This places structural and temporal information into the representation supplied to the Transformer, helping distinguish relationships that unrestricted attention alone would not preserve.

SLATE also uses cross-attention to model relationships between pairs of nodes explicitly, producing edge representations for dynamic link prediction. Across nine datasets, it outperforms numerous leading methods, including message-passing graph networks combined with recurrent models and dynamic graph Transformers. These findings support the combined use of spatiotemporal encoding and explicit pairwise modeling for predicting links in changing graphs.
neurips-2024-supra-laplacian-encoding-fo.tldr: SLATE preserves graph structure and time through supra-Laplacian encodings and models node pairs explicitly for dynamic link prediction.

paragraphs: Community detection finds groups within networks and helps expose their organizational structure without labeled examples. Many traditional methods optimize a specialized objective using a custom search algorithm. This paper brings one established information-theoretic objective, the map equation, into neural learning by rewriting it in a differentiable tensor form.

The reformulation allows gradient descent to optimize the map equation and makes it compatible with neural-network architectures. It supports end-to-end learning and the inclusion of node features, connecting information about individual nodes with the network clustering objective. The authors also state that the formulation automatically selects the optimal number of clusters without requiring explicit regularization.

On synthetic and real-world graph-clustering tasks, the approach achieves competitive performance against leading deep graph-clustering baselines. The finding supports integrating a traditional community-detection objective into modern neural training, rather than establishing superiority across all evaluated methods. The broader contribution is a reusable differentiable formulation that allows network-flow-based community detection to benefit from learned representations and node attributes.
neurips-2024-the-map-equation-goes-neura.tldr: A differentiable map equation enables end-to-end neural graph clustering with node features and automatic selection of the number of clusters.

paragraphs: Safety-aligned language models can fail in either direction: accepting toxic prompts or refusing benign ones. Toxicity detectors also face a difficult trade-off when toxic inputs are rare, because keeping false alarms low can leave many toxic examples undetected. This paper looks for a detection signal inside the language model's own response computation.

Moderation Using LLM Introspection, or MULI, uses the logits for the first response token. These scores describe the model's possible token choices before it begins answering. The authors find that their distribution contains information that distinguishes benign from toxic prompts, and train a sparse logistic regression classifier on those scores.

The resulting detector outperforms state-of-the-art toxicity detectors under multiple metrics in the reported evaluation. The approach matters because it turns information already produced by the language model into a moderation signal, rather than relying solely on whether the final response refuses. Its evidence concerns classification from first-token scores; the title's suggestion of detection for free should be understood through that reuse of model information.
neurips-2024-toxicity-detection-for-free.tldr: MULI detects toxic prompts with a sparse classifier using the language model's first-response-token logits.

paragraphs: A multimodal language model needs a connector that transfers information from its vision encoder to its language model. The quality and computational cost of this bridge affect the resulting system. This paper focuses on improving that connector so visual understanding can remain accurate while requiring less computation.

The authors identify visual anchors within a Vision Transformer and develop an inexpensive search procedure that extracts them progressively. They then introduce Anchor Former, or AcFormer, which uses the pretrained knowledge contained in these anchors to guide information aggregation. The connector therefore builds on informative visual structures already present in the vision encoder.

Extensive experiments show that the proposed method reduces computational costs by nearly two-thirds while outperforming baseline methods. The reported result is notable because improved efficiency accompanies improved performance in those evaluations, rather than a measured accuracy sacrifice. The contribution highlights the connector as a useful target for multimodal-model design and shows that visual anchors can provide effective guidance for gathering the information passed to the language model.
neurips-2024-visual-anchors-are-strong-i.tldr: AcFormer uses visual anchors to guide vision-language information aggregation, reducing computational costs by nearly two-thirds while outperforming baselines.
